newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares end week largely firmer.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares end week largely firmer.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares ended the week on a positive note on Friday, thriving on speculation of a lower than expected May inflation figure, brokers said.
They said a number of investors were also coming into the market to pick up bargains, with a number of counters now at affordable prices.
"We believe the market now has some good value, a number of counters are quite cheap at the moment," commented one broker.
The key industrial index climbed 42.17 points to close at 10,466.73 on Friday, leaping 404.42 points during the week.
The day's advances were in hotel giant Meikles which added 50 cents to 2,750, while clothing retailers Edgars went up 20 cents to 800.
Financial house UDC at 280, blue chip conglomerate Delta at 1,740 and electronic firm Apex at 290 all added 10 cents.
Minings on the other hand were weaker though more active than of late with gold firm Falgold down 15 cents to 60.
Rio Tinto tumbled 300 cents to 2,000 and Ashanti, another gold producer, lost 500 cents to 11,000. The index there went down 42.73 points to close at 954.32 on Friday, losing 9.02 points on the week.
